lead.headline: Home-computer readers wire up for the modem age
lead.dek: BYTE's March 1983 issue put a Bell 103-compatible originate/answer modem project in front of hobbyists as personal-computer communications moved from curiosity toward routine use.
lead.body: During the week of March 14-20, 1983, the computer press kept one eye on telecommunications. BYTE Volume 8 Number 3 listed Steve Ciarcia's Build the ECM-103, an Originate/Answer Modem, a Texas Instruments TMS99532-based Bell 103-compatible project. The article sat beside VIC-20 expansion, COMDEX impressions, storage technology, and retail advertising, a useful snapshot of how hobbyist building, home-computer upgrades, and business microcomputing shared the same magazine rack.
